low: The Sheriff calls before breakfast. "Just checking in," the Sheriff says. It is the first time "just" has ever sounded like a warning.
The Sheriff leaves a note on your door: "People are asking." It is not signed. It does not need to be.
mid: The Sheriff rings at six. "The Courier has a photographer outside the station. I want something to say by noon."
"I need movement," the Sheriff says, on the phone, before you have said hello. "Real movement. The mayor has been in twice."
high: The Sheriff does not say good morning. "The state police are asking for the file," the Sheriff says. "Give me a reason to say no."
The phone rings before you are awake. "They have started locking their doors," says the Sheriff. "The whole town. Do you understand? I can hear it from here."

low: THE COURIER: Residents are asking when the detective will say something.
THE COURIER: A quiet unease on Mercy Street. Doors that were never locked are locked.
mid: THE COURIER: Parents are walking children to school. The word 'safe' is on the lips of everyone and in the heart of no one.
THE COURIER: The hardware store has sold out of locks. The pastor has added a second evening service.
high: THE COURIER: Little Mercy sleeps with the lights on. The detective has 'no comment'.
THE COURIER: Three nights, three bolted doors on every street. The town is counting days with you.

panel_empty: Nothing is about to slip away that you can see. That is not the same as nothing slipping away.
